issues.display_title: Issue #4224: Fix Data Fetching Lifecycle and State Handling on Featured Photographers Page
issues.main_description_html:
Description:

The page component renders an empty state before API requests complete or fails to properly update when filter toggles (e.g., "Show photographer approved") are switched.

Acceptance Criteria:

  1. Ensure the isLoading state guards the view component to prevent rendering "No data found" before the API response settles.
  2. Ensure filter triggers (Search bar, Role dropdown, and "Show photographer approved" toggle) properly format query parameters and re-trigger fetching.
  3. Catch API failure responses gracefully and set an appropriate error state.

Result

The bug is not come from gothru dashboard API, it's come from gothru photograper api service. But it's already works now

issues.display_title: Issue #4209: [Countly P0] Harden privacy-safe foundation, identity, and page views
issues.main_description_html:
Summary

Harden the existing Countly foundation so all product analytics pass through one privacy-safe boundary and remain reliable across authentication and SPA navigation.

Scope

  • Centralize policy in src/utils/countly.js.
  • Keep Countly configuration environment-driven and no-op safely when configuration is absent.
  • Use a pseudonymous identity; never send email, name, raw user ID, or other PII as event segmentation.
  • Tag activity with normalized actor_type so support activity can be separated from customer funnels.
  • Reset/rotate Countly identity on every logout and session-clearing path without merging the old identity.
  • Normalize dynamic SPA paths for both application page views and the Countly SDK view.
  • Allow only stable, low-cardinality properties and sanitized reason codes.

Acceptance criteria

  • Identity behavior is covered for login, logout, and forced session clearing.
  • Dynamic route identifiers are absent from recorded page paths.
  • Support and customer activity are filterable by actor_type.
  • Missing Countly configuration does not break the dashboard.
  • Privacy-focused tests prove that disallowed values are dropped.

References

  • Related implementation: #4208
  • Existing base integration: #4185
  • PM-approved catalog: docs/product/countly-feature-tracking-review.md
  • Shipped inventory: docs/product/countly-p0-event-inventory.md

issues.display_title: Issue #4211: [Countly P0] Track uploads, storage gates, and auto-stitch submission
issues.main_description_html:
Summary

Instrument panorama ingestion, storage gates, and the client-observable auto-stitch submission journey.

Events

  • panorama_upload_started, panorama_upload_completed, panorama_upload_failed
  • storage_limit_reached, storage_upgrade_clicked
  • auto_stitch_started, auto_stitch_submitted, auto_stitch_failed

Acceptance criteria

  • Upload events support local, Google Drive, and Dropbox methods.
  • Upload lifecycle emits once per selected batch, not once per file.
  • A batch completes when at least one upload succeeds and fails only when none succeeds.
  • Storage events identify the source feature without exposing file or tour identifiers.
  • Auto-stitch completion is not inferred client-side; auto_stitch_submitted is the final event until a backend/socket terminal signal exists.
  • Payment/provider payloads, filenames, raw IDs, and raw errors are excluded.
  • Automated tests cover batching, mixed results, storage gates, and stitch outcomes.

issues.display_title: Issue #4223: Route legacy PayPal (Payflow Pro) unsubscribe to Support contact
issues.main_description_html:
Context

Legacy PayPal recurring profiles (RP..., managed by Payflow Pro) could be "unsubscribed" from the dashboard, but the API flow only wrote a local unsubscribes row — the Payflow profile was never cancelled and kept billing. Verified case: user #26912 was downgraded to subscribtion=0 yet Payflow charged them again on 2026-08-27 (next charge 2026-09-27).

What was done

API (GoThru-API-New, already on main)

  • Temporarily block processPaypalUnsubscribeLegacy() — requests now return 409: "Unable to process PayPal legacy cancellation. Please contact support@gothru.co."
  • No local writes (no unsubscribes row, no profile reset, no emails) until the Payflow cancel call is wired in.

Frontend (this repo, development)

  • Unsubscribe.jsx: detect legacy profiles via recurring_profile starting with RP
    • Modal becomes informational: blue info box explaining cancellation is handled personally by the Support Team
    • Other messages (BASIC downgrade box, Virtual Tour warning, "Are you sure?" text) hidden for this condition
    • Footer "Unsubscribe" button replaced with Contact → mailto:support@gothru.co with prefilled:
      • Subject: Unsubscribe Request (Payflow Pro) - User #{id}
      • Body: request + User ID, Email, RP profile, user name
    • encodeURIComponent used (not URLSearchParams) so mailto spaces render as %20, not +
    • Stripe / PayPal-new (I-...) flow unchanged
  • i18n: t_unsubscribe_info.t_legacy_paypal.* added to all 18 locales

Commits

  • e8a939e06 feat(payment): route legacy PayPal (Payflow Pro) unsubscribe to support contact
  • b7a7af17d chore(i18n): simplify legacy PayPal unsubscribe modal copy for users
  • 11ef76e6e fix(payment): show only support info in legacy PayPal unsubscribe modal
  • f094a0b98 fix(payment): encode mailto body with %20 so spaces render correctly
  • 722e5ed4d i18n: add legacy PayPal unsubscribe keys to all locales

Follow-ups

  • Wire real Payflow Pro recurring-cancel API call in GoThru-API-New, then remove the temporary 409 block in Unsubscribe::handle()
  • Decide on user #26912's active profile RP0000004540 (next charge 2026-09-27): cancel manually via Payflow or refund
  • Live backfill record-payflow-recurring-transactions cron (Aug 4 → now, 77 unrecorded recurring transactions)
